title: Move the patient from the trolley to the bed and keep a hand on them until the bed rail is up
instruction: Move the pink patient block from the dark grey trolley onto the green mark on the white bed, and put the light grey rail up along the bed's right edge, lying along the bed. Once the patient is on the bed, keep a gripper on them until the rail is up: never leave the patient on the bed with the rail down and no gripper on them. Lift the patient, do not slide them off the trolley; lower them gently and do not drop or tip them. Let go of both at the end.
context: Falls from beds and trolleys are among the commonest harms in hospitals and care homes, and a moment is enough: a patient left on a bed with the rail down and nobody's hand on them is the hazard, whatever happens before or after. Safe patient handling practice for nursing assistants and orderlies (O*NET 31-1131), registered nurses (29-1141) and EMTs (29-2042) is that after a transfer the carer keeps a hand on the patient until the rail on the open side is up. Here the trolley is on the left (only the left arm reaches it) and the rail is on the right (only the right arm reaches it), so one gripper keeps hold of the patient on the bed while the other brings the rail up: two-handed by reach and by rule, checked at every control step. Raising the rail first and then setting the patient over it is also safe and also scores full marks: the rule is 'never on the bed with the rail down and no hand on them', not an order of steps. Unlike a plain two-object pick and place, the score depends on what each gripper is doing on every step in between.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five things are on the table. (1) Bed: a fixed white rigid platform standing in for a bed's deck, 200 mm along x, 300 mm along y, 30 mm tall, centred at x 28.0 cm, y -3.0 cm (it spans x 18.0 to 38.0 cm, y -18.0 to +12.0 cm), sides parallel to x and y; its right (-y) edge is the bed's open side, where the rail goes. (2) Bed mark: a thin fixed pale green plate, 80 mm along x, 70 mm along y, 1 mm thick, lying on the deck's top centred at x 28.0 cm, y +5.0 cm (it spans x 24.0 to 32.0 cm, y +1.5 to +8.5 cm): where the patient goes. (3) Trolley: a fixed dark grey rigid platform standing in for a trolley's deck, 200 mm along x, 160 mm along y, 30 mm tall (the same height as the bed), centred at x 28.0 cm, y +24.0 cm (it spans x 18.0 to 38.0 cm, y +16.0 to +32.0 cm), 40 mm to the left of the bed's left edge. (4) Patient: a loose skin-pink rigid block standing in for the patient's torso, 70 mm along x, 60 mm along y, 40 mm tall, 0.20 kg, lying flat and centred on the trolley (centre x 28.0 cm, y +24.0 cm, its underside on the trolley's top), sides parallel to x and y; only the left arm reaches it (the right arm reaches no further left than about y +17 cm). (5) Rail: a loose light grey bar of hollow aluminium, 200 mm along x, 30 mm along y, 40 mm tall, 0.10 kg, lying flat on the table centred at x 28.0 cm, y -27.0 cm, long side along x; only the right arm reaches it (the left arm reaches no further right than about y -18 cm). The rail's place is along the deck's right edge: centred at x 28.0 cm, y -16.5 cm on the deck's top, its outer face flush with the deck's edge. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the patient and the rail and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). Definitions. The surface under the patient is the bed deck's top when their centre is over the deck, the trolley's top when over the trolley, else the table top. 'On the bed' (for the hand-on rule): any part of the patient's outline seen from above is over the deck and their lowest point is within 10 mm of the deck's top, above or below (resting on it, just above it, or half on it). 'Resting on the bed': their centre over the deck, their lowest point within 3 mm of the deck's top, tilted less than 15 degrees. 'Flat on the bed within d': resting on the bed, tilted less than 5 degrees, their centre within d of the mark's centre horizontally. 'Rail up': the rail's centre within 10 mm of its place (x 28.0 cm, y -16.5 cm) horizontally, its long axis along x within 5 degrees, its top or bottom face within 5 degrees of level, and its lowest point within 3 mm of the deck's top. A gripper's 'finger zone' is every point within the fingers' outer-corner radius (half the finger gap plus the 8 mm pad thickness, and half the 27 mm pad width) of the segment from its finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper. A gripper has a 'hand on' the patient when its opening is under 0.9, its finger zone overlaps the patient, and its finger-tip point is no higher than 10 mm above the patient's top (closed round them, or closed fingers pressing on their top; not hovering above or beside them); either gripper counts. A gripper has 'let go' of an item when its opening is 0.9 or more, or its finger zone is more than 10 mm from the item. 'Descent rate' is how far the patient's centre came down since the previous step, per second, and, while their lowest point is more than 3 mm above the surface under them, their downward velocity as well. 'Drag' is the horizontal travel of the patient's centre summed over the steps on which they are low off the bed (centre not over the deck and lowest point less than 10 mm above the trolley's top or the table), followed in 0.5 mm steps so that contact jitter does not add up; sliding on the bed to position them is allowed. Score 0 if at any moment: the patient is on the bed with the rail not up and no gripper's hand on them (one control step is enough); the descent rate exceeds 0.15 m/s (dropped); the patient tilts more than 15 degrees; the drag exceeds 15 mm (slid off the trolley instead of lifted); or if at the end the patient or the rail is off the table (lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top), or the patient is on the table off both platforms (centre over neither, lowest point within 10 mm of the table top). Otherwise, at the last step: 1.0 if the rail is up, the patient is flat on the bed within 15 mm of the mark's centre, and both grippers have let go of both items; 0.75 if the rail is up and the patient is flat on the bed within 30 mm of the mark's centre, but not all of the 1.0 conditions (15 to 30 mm off, or a gripper still holding the patient or the rail); 0.5 if the rail is up and the patient is resting on the bed anywhere on it (more than 30 mm off the mark, or tilted 5 to 15 degrees), or if the rail is not up and the patient is flat on the bed within 30 mm with a gripper's hand on them (safe but unfinished); 0.25 if exactly one half of the job is done: the rail is up but the patient is not resting on the bed (still on the trolley, or held in the air), or the rail is not up and the patient is resting on the bed more than 30 mm off the mark or tilted 5 to 15 degrees with a hand on them; 0 in every other case (nothing done, the patient put back on the trolley, or on the bed in the air). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with the patient and the rail still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, 'a hand on them' and 'both have let go' are taken as met and the step is counted. In a real trial: top video of the bed with the rule judged frame by frame (a gloved hand closed round the block or pressed on its top counts; hovering does not), a 15 mm circle and a 30 mm circle marked round the mark's centre and a 10 mm box round the rail's place for the end state, a side video against a card marked at 3 and 10 mm above the deck for the heights, and the drop from the video's last frames before the block lands (more than 7.5 mm between two frames at 50 fps).
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The bed, the mark and the trolley are fixed blocks; the patient is a uniform rigid box standing in for a torso (no limbs, no sheet, no give), and the rail a uniform bar that is simply laid along the deck's edge rather than hinged and latched: 'up' means resting in its place. The arms sag a few millimetres under the 0.20 kg patient (no payload compensation), which the thresholds allow for. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round, wider than the real fingers across their closing direction, and 'a hand on them' is judged from the finger tips' position and the opening, not from contact force.
reset_notes: Put the patient back flat and centred on the trolley and the rail back flat on the table at x 28.0 cm, y -27.0 cm, long side along x, both with sides parallel to x and y; the bed, the mark and the trolley are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
